lessons.title: What Can We Measure?

play.targetObjective: Choose the tool that answers the question: how long, how heavy, or how much it holds.
stepByStep: Listen to the question.
Is it about how long, how heavy, or how much it holds?
Tap the tool that finds out.
play.kidTip: A ruler is for long. A balance is for heavy. A jug is for how much it holds.
play.audioPrompt: What would you use to find out? Tap the tool.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Naming the attribute comes before measuring it: a child who says "bigger" for everything cannot yet choose what to compare.

lessons.title: Longer or Shorter?

play.targetObjective: Pick the longer or the shorter of two things that start at the same line.
stepByStep: Both start at the line.
Look at the other ends.
The one that ends further away is longer.
play.kidTip: Look at the ends. Which one goes further?
play.audioPrompt: Which one is longer, or shorter? Tap it.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Both things start together, so the comparison is only about where they end. The next lesson takes that support away.

lessons.title: Taller or Shorter?

play.targetObjective: Pick the taller or the shorter of two things standing on the same floor.
stepByStep: Both stand on the floor.
Look at the tops.
The one with the higher top is taller.
play.kidTip: They stand on the same floor. Look at the tops.
play.audioPrompt: Which one is taller, or shorter? Tap it.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Height is length standing up. Using the same floor is the vertical version of a shared start line.

lessons.title: Line Them Up

play.targetObjective: Move things to the same start line before saying which is longer.
stepByStep: Find the one that starts late.
Tap it, then tap the start line.
Now compare the ends.
play.kidTip: Start them together before you choose.
play.audioPrompt: Which one is really longer? Line them up first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The shorter thing starts late so its end sticks out further. A child who judges by the far end alone gets it wrong, which is the point.

lessons.title: Shortest to Longest

play.targetObjective: Put three things in order from shortest to longest.
stepByStep: Find the shortest one.
Put it in the first space.
Then the middle one, then the longest.
play.kidTip: Find the shortest one first.
play.audioPrompt: Put them in order, shortest first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Ordering three needs two comparisons held together: shorter than this one, longer than that one.

lessons.title: Use a String

play.targetObjective: Use a string to compare two things that cannot be put side by side.
stepByStep: Hold the string up to the first thing.
Take the string to the second thing.
Is the string longer or shorter?
play.kidTip: The string is as long as the first thing. Compare it with the second.
play.audioPrompt: They cannot move. Use the string to compare them.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Comparing through a third object is the idea a ruler is built on: the string carries one length to the other.

lessons.title: Heavier or Lighter?

play.targetObjective: Use a pan balance to find which of two things is heavier or lighter.
stepByStep: Put both things on the balance.
See which side goes down.
The side that goes down is heavier.
play.kidTip: The heavier side goes down.
play.audioPrompt: Which one is heavier, or lighter? Use the balance.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Half the pairs are big-but-light against small-but-heavy, so a child who judges by size alone is wrong half the time. The balance, not the eye, decides.

lessons.title: Which Holds More?

play.targetObjective: Pour two containers into cups to find which one holds more.
stepByStep: Pour the first one into cups.
Pour the second one into cups.
The one that fills more cups holds more.
play.kidTip: Count the cups. More cups means it holds more.
play.audioPrompt: Which one holds more? Pour each into cups.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Tall containers look as if they hold more. Most rounds pair a tall one that holds less with a wide one that holds more, so counting cups beats looking.

lessons.title: Measure with Blocks

play.targetObjective: Measure a length by laying blocks end to end with no gaps, then counting them.
stepByStep: Start at the end of the thing.
Lay each block right after the last one.
Stop at the other end and count the blocks.
play.kidTip: No gaps, no overlaps. Then count.
play.audioPrompt: How many blocks long is it? Lay blocks along it.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The child lays every block, so the number is earned by covering the length, not read off a label. The count is never printed on screen.

lessons.title: Spot the Mistake

play.targetObjective: Tell a proper measurement from one with a gap or an overlap.
stepByStep: Look at both rows of blocks.
Find the row with no gaps and no overlaps.
Count the blocks in that row.
play.kidTip: Blocks must touch end to end.
play.audioPrompt: Which row is measured right? Then count it.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A gap gives too small a number and an overlap too big a one. Seeing someone else's mistake is easier than seeing your own, so it comes first.

lessons.title: Big Unit, Small Unit

play.targetObjective: Explain that a smaller unit needs more of them to measure the same length.
stepByStep: Look at the cubes and the rods.
Both measure the same thing.
The smaller unit needs more.
play.kidTip: Small units, more of them. Big units, fewer.
play.audioPrompt: Which needs more: cubes or rods?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The inverse relation between unit size and count is the idea behind every later conversion: 1 m is 100 cm because a centimetre is small.

lessons.title: Balance with Cubes

play.targetObjective: Find how many cubes weigh the same as a thing by making the balance level.
stepByStep: Put cubes on the other pan.
Add or take off cubes.
When the beam is level, count the cubes.
play.kidTip: Level beam means the same weight.
play.audioPrompt: How many cubes weigh the same? Make it balance.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The same idea as blocks along a length: a mass is measured by how many equal units match it.

lessons.title: Fill with Cups

play.targetObjective: Measure how much a container holds by pouring it into cups and counting them.
stepByStep: Pour it into cups.
Count the full cups.
That is how many cups it holds.
play.kidTip: Count each full cup.
play.audioPrompt: How many cups does it fill? Pour it out.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Capacity measured in equal cups, ready for millilitres and litres later.

lessons.title: Read the Ruler

play.targetObjective: Read a length in centimetres when the thing starts at 0.
stepByStep: Find the 0 on the ruler.
Look where the thing ends.
That number is how long it is.
play.kidTip: Start at 0. Read the end.
play.audioPrompt: How long is it? Read the ruler.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A ruler is the blocks from Unit 157 with numbers written on. The number at the end only gives the length because the thing starts at 0.

lessons.title: Measure It

play.targetObjective: Line a thing up with the 0 mark, not the edge of the ruler, then read it.
stepByStep: Pick up the thing.
Put its end on 0, not the edge.
Read the number at the other end.
play.kidTip: The edge is not 0. Find the 0 mark.
play.audioPrompt: Measure it. Put it on the 0 first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: On most rulers the 0 sits a little in from the edge. Children who start at the edge are out by a few millimetres, and on a cheap ruler by a whole centimetre.

lessons.title: Draw a Line

play.targetObjective: Draw a line of a given length in centimetres, starting at 0.
stepByStep: Start the line at 0.
Find the number you need.
Draw to that mark.
play.kidTip: Start at 0, stop at the number.
play.audioPrompt: Draw a line. Start at 0.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Drawing is reading backwards: the child knows the length and finds the mark. It checks they understand where a length starts.

lessons.title: Broken Ruler

play.targetObjective: Measure with a ruler that does not start at 0 by counting the spaces.
stepByStep: Look at the number where the thing starts.
Count the spaces to the end.
Or take the start number from the end number.
play.kidTip: Count the spaces, not the marks.
play.audioPrompt: This ruler is broken. How long is it?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The end number is the classic wrong answer here, so it is always one of the choices. Counting spaces, not marks, is the idea behind every scale later.

lessons.title: How Much Longer?

play.targetObjective: Find how much longer one thing is than another by measuring both.
stepByStep: Read the long one.
Read the short one.
Take the short length from the long length.
play.kidTip: Measure both, then subtract.
play.audioPrompt: How much longer is one than the other?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Both lengths are on offer as wrong answers, because naming a length is the common slip. The green gap in the hint is the difference itself.

lessons.title: cm or m?

play.targetObjective: Choose cm, m or km to measure an everyday length.
stepByStep: Think how big the thing is.
Small things are measured in cm.
Big things in m, and long trips in km.
play.kidTip: Small: cm. Big: m. Far: km.
play.audioPrompt: Which unit would you use?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Units are chosen by size, so each unit is asked about equally often and 'm' is never the safe guess.

lessons.title: About How Long?

play.targetObjective: Estimate a length by picking the sensible amount.
stepByStep: Picture the thing.
Compare it with something you know.
Pick the amount that makes sense.
play.kidTip: A door is about 2 m tall.
play.audioPrompt: About how long is it? Pick the one that makes sense.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The wrong answer is always ten times off, so this is about sense of size, not exact digits. Benchmarks (a finger is 1 cm, a big step is 1 m) are the tool.

lessons.title: Lengths on a Number Line

play.targetObjective: Add and take away lengths by jumping along a number line.
stepByStep: Find the starting length.
Jump right to add, left to take away.
Read where you land.
play.kidTip: Right to add, left to take away.
play.audioPrompt: Start at the first length. Jump. Where do you land?

lessons.pedagogyTip: A number line is a ruler without the thing. It links measuring to adding and subtracting within 100.

lessons.title: Inches and Feet

play.targetObjective: Read a length in whole inches on a 1-foot ruler.
stepByStep: Find the 0.
Look where the thing ends.
Read the inches. 12 inches make 1 foot.
play.kidTip: 12 inches make 1 foot.
play.audioPrompt: How long is it in inches?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Same skill as centimetres on a bigger unit. Only US learners see inches; elsewhere the metric ruler carries on.

lessons.title: Half and Quarter Inches

play.targetObjective: Read a length to the nearest half or quarter inch.
stepByStep: Find the last whole inch.
Count the small parts after it.
2 parts make a half; 1 part is a quarter.
play.kidTip: Each inch has 4 small parts.
play.audioPrompt: How long is it? Count the small parts.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A ruler is a number line of fractions. The mirror mistake (¼ for ¾) is always offered, because reading from the wrong mark is the usual slip.

lessons.title: Measure in mm

play.targetObjective: Read a length in millimetres, using 1 cm = 10 mm.
stepByStep: Find the last cm before the end.
That many cm is that many tens of mm.
Count the small marks after it.
play.kidTip: 1 cm is 10 mm.
play.audioPrompt: How long is it in mm? Count the small marks.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The zoom lens magnifies the one centimetre where the thing ends, so the marks can be counted on a phone. Being out by 10 means a cm was read as a mm.

lessons.title: g or kg?
lessons.concept: Choosing Units of Mass and Capacity

play.targetObjective: Choose g or kg to weigh a thing, and ml or l to measure how much it holds.
stepByStep: Think how heavy it is, or how much it holds.
Light things: g. Heavy things: kg.
A little drink: ml. A lot of water: l.
play.kidTip: Light: g. Heavy: kg.
play.audioPrompt: Which unit would you use?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The same idea as cm or m, now for mass and capacity. Each unit is the answer equally often.

lessons.title: Read the Scale

play.targetObjective: Read a weight in grams from a scale where every mark has a number.
stepByStep: Look where the needle points.
Read the number there.
Say it in grams.
play.kidTip: Follow the needle to the number.
play.audioPrompt: How much does it weigh? Read the scale.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A round scale is a ruler bent into a circle. Here every mark is numbered, so the only new thing is the needle.

lessons.title: Scale Steps

play.targetObjective: Work out what each unnumbered mark is worth, then read the scale.
stepByStep: Find two numbers next to each other.
Count the steps between them.
Share the gap by the steps, then count on from the number before the needle.
play.kidTip: How much is one small mark?
play.audioPrompt: How much does it weigh? Work out the small marks first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Steps of 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100 and 250 all appear. Counting the marks as 1s is the usual slip, so that answer is always offered.

lessons.title: Kilogram Scales

play.targetObjective: Read a bathroom scale in kilograms and a luggage scale in half kilograms.
stepByStep: Find the number before the needle.
Work out what each mark is worth.
Count on to the needle.
play.kidTip: Find the number, then count the marks.
play.audioPrompt: How heavy is it? Read the scale.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Real scales a child meets at home and at the airport. Luggage scales mark halves, so ½ kg is read as a mark, not a fraction sum.

lessons.title: Pounds and Ounces

play.targetObjective: Read a weight in pounds and ounces, using 16 oz = 1 lb.
stepByStep: Find the last pound before the needle.
Count the ounces after it.
Say it as pounds and ounces.
play.kidTip: 16 ounces make 1 pound.
play.audioPrompt: How much does it weigh, in pounds and ounces?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Only US learners see pounds. Every ounce has a mark and every 4 ounces a longer one, so a quarter pound is easy to find.

lessons.title: Read the Jug

play.targetObjective: Read how much water is in a measuring jug, in millilitres.
stepByStep: Look at the top of the water.
Find the number before it.
Count the marks up to the water.
play.kidTip: Read at the top of the water.
play.audioPrompt: How much water is in the jug?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The marks step down over the round: 100s, then 50s, then 25s, so the child meets unnumbered marks one size at a time.

lessons.title: Fill to the Line

play.targetObjective: Pour water into a jug until it reaches the amount asked for.
stepByStep: Find the amount on the jug.
Pour in until the water reaches it.
Pour out a little if you go past.
play.kidTip: Stop when the water meets the line.
play.audioPrompt: Fill the jug to the line.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Measuring out is the reverse of reading. Pouring in big and small steps teaches the marks by doing.

lessons.title: Cups, Pints, Quarts, Gallons

play.targetObjective: Know how many cups, pints and quarts fill a bigger container.
stepByStep: 2 cups fill a pint.
2 pints fill a quart.
4 quarts fill a gallon.
play.kidTip: 2 cups, 2 pints, 4 quarts.
play.audioPrompt: How many fill it?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Only US learners see these. The containers are drawn to scale so the doubling can be seen, not just remembered.

lessons.title: Read the Thermometer

play.targetObjective: Read a temperature in degrees Celsius.
stepByStep: Find the top of the red line.
Find the number below it.
Count up the marks.
play.kidTip: Read at the top of the red line.
play.audioPrompt: What temperature does it show?

lessons.pedagogyTip: A thermometer is a scale standing up. The marks go 1s, then 2s, then 5s over the round.

lessons.title: Below Zero

play.targetObjective: Read temperatures below zero.
stepByStep: Find the 0 on the thermometer.
Below 0 the numbers count down: −1, −2, −3.
Read the top of the red line.
play.kidTip: Below zero, bigger numbers are colder.
play.audioPrompt: What temperature does it show? It may be below zero.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Cold places and freezers. The sign slip (3 for −3) is always offered as a choice, because it is the usual mistake.

lessons.title: Warmer, Colder

play.targetObjective: Work out a new temperature after it gets warmer or colder, crossing zero.
stepByStep: Start at the first temperature.
Warmer goes up; colder goes down.
Count the degrees, past 0 if you need to.
play.kidTip: Warmer: up. Colder: down.
play.audioPrompt: It got warmer or colder. What is it now?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Most changes cross 0, the hard part. Going the wrong way is offered as a choice so the direction is checked.

lessons.title: Fahrenheit

play.targetObjective: Read a temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.
stepByStep: Find the top of the red line.
Find the number below it.
Each mark is 2 degrees: count up.
play.kidTip: Each mark is 2 degrees.
play.audioPrompt: What temperature does it show, in °F?

lessons.pedagogyTip: US weather is given in °F. Same reading skill, with marks of 2.

lessons.title: Add and Subtract Measures

play.targetObjective: Solve word problems that add or subtract amounts in the same unit.
stepByStep: Read the story.
Is it put together, taken away, or a difference?
Add or subtract, and give the unit.
play.kidTip: Together: add. Taken away or how much more: subtract.
play.audioPrompt: Read the story. Add or subtract.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Lengths, masses and capacities, all in one unit. The wrong operation is always a choice; the bar model hint shows which one is right.

lessons.title: Practice: Scales

play.shortDesc: Kitchen scales, marks in steps, kilograms and pounds, in turn.
play.targetObjective: No hints, no explanations, no voice. Just the questions.
stepByStep: The techniques you have learned, mixed together.
Nothing is read aloud and there are no hints.
Work each one out, and see how many you get first time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice is retrieval, not instruction, and it is open from the start: a child who already knows a technique should not have to sit through the lesson to get at the questions. The help is removed on purpose — recalling something unaided is a different act from being walked through it, and it is the one that makes it stick.

play.targetObjective: No hints, no explanations, no voice. Just the questions.
